title: React and react-dom versions differ in the rejected lockfile
currentSourceReason: The proposal resolved React 19.2.6 and react-dom 19.2.4. It never merged; the audit baseline resolved both to 18.3.1. This was source-confirmed against React's version requirement, not an executed historical installation.

title: Local SVG use references could recurse through ancestor or mutual cycles
currentSourceReason: The baseline parser tracks active references and limits expansion/depth; current structure tests cover circular references and bounded fan-out. Historical source was inspected, but an old packaged app was not run.

title: Unstyled SVG shapes lost their default black fill
currentSourceReason: Baseline visibleFill restores black paint for shapes while keeping lines unfilled. Existing stylesheet tests compare unstyled geometry with explicit black fill.

title: An SVG child could not restore visible visibility below a hidden ancestor
currentSourceReason: The baseline separates inherited visibility from hiddenSubtree used for display/group opacity. Existing structure tests cover the distinction.

title: Asynchronous material-library export can clear a later dirty marker
currentSourceReason: The saved callback race was observed in source, but baseline persistence independently saves document changes and the report found no production consumer of this marker beyond state plumbing. No user-visible loss was demonstrated; the race was not proved harmless in all future uses.

title: Legacy-library migration removed the old slot after a failed destination write
currentSourceReason: Baseline migration requires successful collection persistence and exact readback before removing the legacy slot. Both quota-failure and mismatched-readback regressions passed; historical behaviour was source-derived.

title: Desktop keep-awake requests were silently denied
currentSourceReason: The baseline Electron policy permits screen-wake-lock and the hook emits a single visible notice on denial/missing support. Six hook tests passed; native OS sleep behaviour was not exercised.

title: Unsigned packaged builds could automatically install mutable-feed updates
currentSourceReason: Baseline auto-update requires a trusted channel before enabling automatic download/install. The report identifies fcdd00212764b348e25e56bd441117d142e3b310 and ADR-135; the later #54 review confirms that trust separation. No native installer/provider exercise was performed.

title: Malformed-image guard returns the original invalid input
currentSourceReason: The guard's return behaviour was inspected, but the audit did not establish a user-reachable failure through the full trace pipeline. Permissive canvas stubs do not establish rendered correctness, so this is an unproved lead rather than a clean bill of health.

title: Camera bridge accepted requests without an Origin header
currentSourceReason: The baseline rejects missing Origin and validates Host before dispatch. The report attributes the missing-Origin repair to fea8880717aed7bfc57b5f7484b759c99db9f3f4; current policy tests passed without contacting a camera.

title: Surfacing row/pass caps still imply full product materialisation
currentSourceReason: The report notes that the historical emitter materialised the rows-by-passes product, but baseline output is replayable and streamed. No current failure was confirmed; the report does not provide a historical memory-exhaustion runtime reproduction.

title: Surfacing shallow depth was forced up to 0.05 mm
currentSourceReason: The report's baseline comparison says shallow-depth handling preserves the requested depth instead of the historical 0.05 mm floor. This is a source/test disposition, with no material-cut evidence or repair commit identified there.

title: Historical GRBL write/ACK ordering and zero-coordinate jog faults
currentSourceReason: The report says baseline untracked-ACK/safe-write reservation and command/status paths address those historical issues. This is a grouped report-level summary: exact original triggers and repair commits were not itemised, and the whole controller state graph was not audited.

title: West multi-selection resize handle used the eastward formula
currentSourceReason: The baseline uses x:west instead of historical x:east and has all-handle regressions. The report identifies c18e6af18 / #494 as the repair.

title: HTTP camera image size was checked only after buffering the full body
currentSourceReason: Baseline camera-frame-body.ts bounds and cancels the stream while reading instead of awaiting response.arrayBuffer before checking 8 MiB. The report identifies the later #792 / 7d4b82812 change.

title: RTSP single-frame capture settled before stdout closed
currentSourceReason: Baseline capture waits for child close rather than exit and releases the slot at that point; existing RTSP stream tests passed. This is separate from the preview URL defect repaired during this audit.

title: Broad internal arc-radius tolerance permits malformed arcs
currentSourceReason: The 0.127 mm internal radius tolerance was investigated, but no reachable UI/caller case with an arbitrary malformed payload was established. It was not promoted without a production trigger/reproduction; no controller execution was performed.

title: Fit discarded nonuniform resized proportions
currentSourceReason: The original helper replaced both scales with one absolute scale. Baseline code multiplies existing scales uniformly; the report identifies #723 / 0580260ba and passing proportional-fit/store-Undo tests.

title: Fit/array does not support zero-width or zero-height line artwork
currentSourceReason: The baseline helper tests explicitly record this unsupported geometry. The audit did not classify it as a newly confirmed defect or establish a broader geometry failure.

title: Circle-board fit used the bounding square
currentSourceReason: This began as an explicit initial limitation. #45 installs diameter/sqrt(2) inscribed-square fitting, used by both baseline Fit and Array paths; current tests passed. This is separate from the later #304 correction/Undo ownership defect.

title: Legacy rotary raster refusal and surface-calibrated roller-only mapping
currentSourceReason: These historical design limits were superseded before the audit: ADR-315 permits producible rotary raster G-code and ADR-373 adds measured roller diameter. They are not current requirements or new bug repairs, and must not be restored on the strength of old documentation.

title: Rotary surface speed and dose vary with motion direction
currentSourceReason: ADR-501 explicitly defines surface speed using emitted feed times the surface/machine path-length ratio. Baseline group speed is machine feed; the report checked the numerical examples and did not treat direction-dependent dose as a contract violation.

title: Ruida layer minimum and maximum power are equal
currentSourceReason: #49 explicitly accepts Min==Max; baseline part records derive both from group.power. A self-generated byte golden proves stability only, not physical acceptance or reference-application equivalence.

title: Legacy homography alignment and Labs gating treated as current camera requirements
currentSourceReason: ADR-440 deleted the old homography/checkerboard/marker modules and Camera alignment v2 switch. Baseline overlay/trace uses the saved lens/pose model, and Print and Cut checks draft targets and coordinate ownership. The old modules/gates do not establish a current defect; the replacement solver and physical optical accuracy were not fully audited.

title: Sub-pixel contour interpolation averaged varying thresholds
currentSourceReason: Baseline contour-boundary.ts interpolates luma-minus-threshold residuals, locating their zero rather than averaging local thresholds. The report identifies repair 2613ff0deb884e8d3935f74df335e45997aafdd3. This is distinct from the closing-fairing seam repaired during this audit.

title: Momentary Fire cleared uncertain state early and emitted incorrect modal/power commands
currentSourceReason: Historical code cleared its latch before off-write success, used bare M3 and rounded fractional S upward. Baseline code preserves uncertain-on state, emits modal G1/F and floors the power share. The report groups these related corrections; no hardware proof is claimed.

title: Quick-nest duplicate free rectangles cause an invalid or lost layout
currentSourceReason: The recorded deterministic search covered 100,000 one-item obstacle cases without reproducing the duplicate-free-rectangle hypothesis. That bounded negative result does not prove general nesting optimality or correctness.

title: Preview/worker cache retention causes a production-lifetime failure
currentSourceReason: The report explicitly withheld an actionable cache-retention finding because production-lifetime proof was missing. It records no confirmed user-visible failure; this is insufficient evidence, not a demonstrated resolution.

title: Manual CNC tool change failed to stop and restart coolant
currentSourceReason: Baseline cnc-grbl-transitions handles coolant stop/restart, with modal/coolant tests. The report contrasts it with the original omission; physical relay, spindle and controller behaviour were not qualified.

title: Retract-first raw-line CNC recovery remains executable
currentSourceReason: #82 removed/disabled that path: baseline buildResumeProgram rejects machineKind=cnc before parsing. ADR-215 introduced a distinct sealed semantic pass-boundary recovery job. Removed preamble concerns are not a current-code finding, and the newer recovery pipeline was only partly reviewed.

title: Finish-only narrow features disappeared or bypassed the depth ladder
currentSourceReason: Baseline finish-allowance coverage/compiler routing follows ADR-140 Amendment 1: finish-only layers survive empty roughing and step down. The report records five ladder and four coverage tests passing.

title: A collapsed machine rail during a job violates the old forced-open policy
currentSourceReason: ADR-139 amendments/ADR-207 permit independent rail visibility with live controls elsewhere. The old force-visible policy is superseded, so restoring it is not justified as a current repair. The full modern shell/native focus behaviour was not qualified.

title: Variable sequence wrap and transient range edits violated integer bounds
currentSourceReason: Baseline bounded wrap uses BigInt for exact safe-integer arithmetic; range controls use DraftNumberInput and clamp sequence-end enabling. These prior corrections are separate from B03-VAR-001's unsafe current-value Counter, which was a new audit finding.

title: Outline nesting can lose a valid arrangement above its work threshold
currentSourceReason: The real store/worker fails for 33 complementary triangles despite a validated layout in 170 by 10 mm; 32 fit. ADR-151 explicitly switches to rectangular fallback above 32 items or 250,000 point-weighted work. The reviewed worker wording says no complete valid arrangement was found, not that one is impossible. Two reviewers accepted this as a bounded heuristic limit.

title: Full-circle GRBL helix emission was ambiguous
currentSourceReason: Baseline cnc-grbl-helical.ts emits two half-circle arcs per revolution. The report inspected #898 / 91c1adefa02c9f24231c7a909f2a97de0c0fd2e7 as the correction, without repeating controller execution. This is separate from the concave-containment defect repaired during this audit.

title: Original rest-machining diameter model does not simulate actual swept stock
currentSourceReason: The report treats ADR-153's diameter-based reachable-stock model as its stated original scope, not a physical stock-simulation promise. Later swept-stock simulation and physical residual-stock measurement were outside this review; no current failure was reproduced from this limitation.

title: Straight-inlay inside corners interfered
currentSourceReason: Baseline inlay-pair.ts performs closing then opening (+r, -2r, +r) before splitting fit allowance. The report identifies #898 / 91c1adefa02c9f24231c7a909f2a97de0c0fd2e7 and passing geometry/compile tests; no physical fit claim was made.

title: Saving rejected valid manual-tab arrays larger than 512 anchors
currentSourceReason: Baseline structural validation has no anchor-count cap, so the reported 140-contour by four-anchor example is no longer rejected by length. The correction is 160ca336dbfe04cd589daab292a179219f5242bc; this differs from the explicit-operation-binding tab defect repaired during this audit.

title: Preview playback uses uniform pacing within a motion category
currentSourceReason: Historical acceptance explicitly permits category-weighted approximate playback rather than exact controller-segment replay. The audit did not establish a violated promise from uniform within-category timing. This differs from WUX-001's unrelated-project timing ownership defect.

title: Hold-jog cleanup cancelled presses on rerender and ignored cancellation capability
currentSourceReason: Baseline useHoldJog uses stable callbacks, argsRef and holdEnabled. The report identifies ebbaf3dd1 / #169 and 95a3ea800 as intervening repairs and records the ten-case JogPad suite passing; physical jog cancellation was not qualified.

title: Origin completion could update state after controller-session ownership changed
currentSourceReason: Baseline runOriginTransaction binds controller session, write epoch and operation identity, applying only owned success/failure patches. The origin suite passed. This prior session-ownership repair is distinct from later #110 tool ownership defect MTX-001 found in this audit.

title: Current SVG repair prematurely censors intermediate Infinity and NaN
currentSourceReason: Review comment r4240505330 did not reproduce at published head 282b60d3c71320ad7884299d7d40924ab59c73f8. All 25 independent Chrome/math controls passed through both parser routes and exact state, including infinity / infinity becoming NaN and outer opacity zero. Six direct @csstools/css-calc 2.1.4 controls using the exact current options preserve numeric Infinity, -Infinity, NaN and signed zero. No math production change is justified by this claim. This is bounded evidence for the reported expressions, not general CSS conformance.

title: Flex-unit cancellation in opacity has conflicting specification and browser support
currentSourceReason: Comment r4240569210 reports calc(1fr / 1fr). Both Chrome154 and the published importer reject that exact expression and preserve the valid lower declaration. CSS Values4 draft type algebra includes flex cancellation while CSS Grid2 retains a flex-in-calc restriction note. The importer retains its observed browser-compatible unsupported-flex boundary; this is not a claim of universal CSS invalidity or a repaired ratio. Independent review separately confirmed sign(1fr) could evade that boundary; that defect is repaired and recorded under FND-001.

title: Relative-unit sign expressions retain the disclosed opaque approximation
currentSourceReason: Comment r4240648358 correctly observes sign(-1em) can clamp to zero while imported geometry is retained. This is covered by the existing explicit layout-dependent opacity-1 approximation and warning that hidden source artwork may be included. Independent normal/zero-font/signed controls preserve that documented behavior. The importer does not perform sign-domain or range analysis to prove every simplifiable contextual expression; this remains a precision limitation, not a repaired expression or browser-equality claim.

title: Stylesheet revert-layer is alleged to bypass SVG presentation attributes
currentSourceReason: The reported literal stylesheet revert-layer plus zero presentation attribute remains hidden in actual Chrome154, matching the importer. All 36 independent rollback assertions pass, including importance and parent controls. Cascade5 distinguishes the author presentational-hint origin for cascading; the comment assumption that the two sources must form one removable layer is not supported by these observations. No rollback production change is justified by this report; arbitrary named layers remain outside the importer scope.

title: Typed attr XML reserialization fails only in the jsdom test environment
currentSourceReason: A raw probe using XML-escaped type(<number>) inside an inline attribute encountered an XML reparse error after jsdom serialization emitted a literal less-than character. Actual Chrome154 with the same installed DOMPurify and sanitizer options preserves the escape and reparses cleanly. This is recorded separately from the 39 substantive attr/importance probe failures; no production sanitizer repair or weakened sanitization is justified by the environment-only result.

title: Concurrently upgrade declares a Node version above historical tooling
currentSourceReason: package-lock concurrently.engines.node >=22; historical workflows select Node20; electron:dev invokes concurrently. Declared toolchain inconsistency. No install or runtime failure reproduced; ordinary CI does not invoke electron:dev. Current manifest and scripts no longer use concurrently; historical PR closed unmerged.

title: Licence checker upgrade exceeds the Node version used by its workflow
currentSourceReason: package-lock checker.engines requires Node>=24/npm>=11; historical license-check workflow selects Node20 and runs scripts/license-check.mjs wrapper. Source-confirmed violation of declared package Node contract; no runtime crash or npm-install failure asserted. Current license-check runs pnpm-aware scripts/check-licenses.mjs and does not depend on license-checker-rseidelsohn; historical PR closed unmerged.

title: Original checkpoint test weak baseline superseded by baseline-relative current test and expanded recovery checks; software score remains historical.
currentSourceReason: Original checkpoint test weak baseline superseded by baseline-relative current test and expanded recovery checks; software score remains historical.

currentSourceReason: Atomic commit arithmetic correct under declared geometry; current geometry/ownership/G92 fixes in 06e8678f3, bb6c54fe5 and 53e6568d1. No duplicate repair.

currentSourceReason: bfef38a93 added toggle; 9721cc783 introduced richer settings. Current action/deserializer synchronize reduceTravelMoves/travelPolicy; independent exact emission controls pass.
